name: opencode
look: Monospace across every text role on one warm cream sheet, ASCII bracket bullets, and a single dark TUI mockup.

hero.title: the coding agent that lives in your terminal
hero.sub: no editor fork, no extension, no browser tab. a TUI that reads your repo, runs your tests, and shows every command before it runs it.

features.title: built for people who already live in a terminal
features.sub: no gui, no account, no cloud state. it reads the repo on disk and edits files in place.

items.title: tui first
items.body: a full-screen terminal interface with panes, scrollback and vim keybindings. runs fine over ssh.

items.title: diffs before writes
items.body: every edit is shown as a diff and applied only when you accept it. nothing is written silently.

items.title: any model
items.body: openai, anthropic, google, or a local endpoint. bring your own key and it never touches ours.

items.title: repo aware
items.body: builds a local index of the tree, so a question about one file knows about its callers.

items.title: runs your tests
items.body: executes the command you configure, reads the failure, and iterates until it passes or you stop it.

items.title: no telemetry
items.body: zero network calls except to the model provider you configured. verify it with tcpdump.

showcases.title: every command shown before it runs
showcases.body: the agent proposes a command, you see it, you approve or reject. no hidden shell execution, and a full transcript of what ran is written to the session log.

showcases.title: mit licensed, all of it
showcases.body: the whole binary is open source under mit, including the agent loop. there is no hosted component and no paid core — the paid tier is a managed model proxy, and it is optional.

gallery.title: [ docs ]
gallery.sub: install, configuration, keybindings and the agent protocol.

testimonial.quote: i ran it over ssh on a box with no gui and it just worked. that is a low bar that almost nothing else in this category clears.
testimonial.name: sam okafor

pricing.title: [ pricing ]
pricing.sub: the tool is free. the optional proxy is not.

items.a: no. the oss build reads a provider key from your environment and never contacts us. an account exists only for the optional managed proxy.
yes, that is the point. it is a terminal program with no gui dependency, so it runs on a headless box the same as on a laptop.

items.q: can it use a local model?
items.a: yes. point it at any openai-compatible endpoint, including a local runtime, and it works identically.
a session transcript and a local index under the project directory, both gitignored by default. nothing else.

cta.title: [ install ]
cta.sub: one binary, no account, mit licensed.

footer.tagline: a coding agent that lives in your terminal.

notes: Every text role is monospace. There is no sans-serif anywhere in the chrome, and introducing one breaks the entire identity.
One warm cream body background across the whole page — no surface alternation between sections.
A single dark surface exists, reserved exclusively for the hero TUI mockup.
ASCII bracket markers ([+], [-], [x]) serve as bullet glyphs in feature lists and FAQ rows.
Interactive elements take a 4px radius; sections themselves are sharp rectangles separated by 1px hairlines with no decorative dividers.
